instruction: Enable auto-save every 7 minutes and turn on 'Always create backup copy' in LibreOffice options.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent successfully navigated to Tools > Options > Load/Save > General, enabled auto-save checkbox, changed interval from 10 to 3 minutes, and clicked OK.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate LibreOffice menus, open Options dialog, navigate dialog tree, enable/disable checkboxes, change numeric spinbox values, confirm with OK
metadata.task_rationale: Multi-step variation combining two settings on the same Load/Save > General page: auto-save interval AND backup copy. Tests model's ability to make multiple changes in one dialog visit.
metadata.explanation: Task requires enabling auto-save at 7 minutes AND enabling 'Always create backup copy'. Custom getter reads registrymodifications.xcu for both AutoSaveTimeIntervall and CreateBackup values. Custom metric awards partial credit: 0.5 for correct auto-save, 0.5 for backup enabled.

scoring_breakdown.auto_save_interval: 0.5 - AutoSave enabled and set to 7 minutes

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads registrymodifications.xcu and extracts AutoSave, AutoSaveTimeIntervall, and CreateBackup properties — the right file and right settings for this task.
Metric correctly handles expected parameter for type='rule' — directly accesses expected.get('expected_minutes') and expected.get('expected_backup') without incorrectly nesting into 'rules'.
Full coverage: both instruction requirements (auto-save at 7 minutes AND backup copy enabled) are verified with appropriate partial credit (0.5 each).
Expected values (expected_minutes=7, expected_backup=true) correctly match the instruction requirements.
No postconfig needed since getter reads a persistent config file, not a transient UI dialog.

Minor concern: regex patterns for XML parsing assume specific element ordering and whitespace in registrymodifications.xcu; unusual formatting could cause false negatives, but this is a minor practical risk for the standard LibreOffice config format.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider using an XML parser (e.g., xml.etree.ElementTree) instead of regex for more robust parsing of registrymodifications.xcu, to handle variations in XML formatting.
